Under the standard text-spacing override the headline 'A world of sound, in color.' runs past the window's right edge, and the hero's overflow: hidden cuts it off. findings.claim:
C6i-1 passes SC 2.5.8 by box geometry, which is the gate's test, the lane's and axe's. It does not pass by the region that really takes a tap.

With padding-block 0, the first text line of a two-line name pokes about 1 px above its own box. That strip wins hit-testing over the bottom of the 24 px name above it. The two-line names are 'Hemisphere in Ember' at 412-441 and 'Mantle in Ember' at 412-428.

What really takes a tap:
- 'Tropos in Acid': 22-23 px at 414-441 (19 px at 412-413).
- 'Core in Ember': 23 px at 414-428.

Under WCAG's own rule (overlapping areas are left out), those two names still fail 2.5.8, Tropos at 412-441 and Core at 412-428. At 412-413 the spacing exception, which had zero margin by boxes, fails too: the 3.5 px gap shrinks to about 1 px between the real regions.

This is not worse than OLD. OLD's real regions are 19-23.75 px and fail for Tropos and Core at 412-441 and for Mantle at 429-434. The only exception is Tropos at 439-441, smaller by at most 0.75 px. It concerns exact squares only, and a tap landing in the bottom 1.5-2 px of a 24 px name. So the lane's 'fails at no whole name' holds by boxes only.
findings.evidence:
Real touchscreen taps (taps.js). A capture listener on window records the link and stops navigation. Each visible name box was tapped 2 px inside its top, at its centre and 2 px inside its bottom, at 412-441 and 463-504.
- NEW: 19 of 864 taps reach the wrong name. OLD: 0 of 864.
- 'Tropos in Acid' bottom goes to Hemisphere at 417-422, 429-434 and 441.
- 'Core in Ember' bottom goes to Mantle at 417-422.

At 417 (tapdbg.js):
- NEW: Tropos box y 135.53-159.53, Hemisphere 159.53-193.53. elementFromPoint at y 158.03 (1.5 px inside Tropos) returns Hemisphere, and so does a touch at 157.53. A mouse click at 157.53 still reaches Tropos.
- OLD: Tropos 138.28-158.09. Hemisphere takes over only 0.5 px inside Tropos, because OLD's Hemisphere has 1.4 px of padding.

Hit scan (hitscan.js: elementFromPoint every 0.25 px down five lines per name; out/hitscan-{new,old}.jsonl):
- NEW's two-line names reach 1.75-1.95 px above their boxes at 414-441; OLD's names 0.8-1.0 px.
- Strict 2.5.8 on the real regions: NEW fails Tropos at 412-441 and Core at 412-428. OLD fails Tropos and Core at 412-441 and Mantle at 429-434.

A remedy tested in my browser only: '@media (aspect-ratio: 1/1) and (min-width: 412px) and (max-width: 441px) { .hero-names a { clip-path: inset(0 -8px -8px) } }'.
- At 414-441 it makes each region equal its box, and 360 of 360 taps reach the right name.
- It changes no pixel without focus.
- With a name focused, it shifts about one pixel row (91-116 px) of the ring's top edge at 13 of 35 squares (pixdiff.js).
- 412-413 still fails strictly.
So it is not a drop-in fix.

findings.where: How C6i-4 was tested. The gate's shared servers on ports 4183-4187 use gate/serve.js.
findings.claim: The lane says headless Chromium does not restore pages from the back/forward cache. That is not right. It does restore once three things change. Launch with chromium.launch({channel:'chromium', ignoreDefaultArgs:['--disable-back-forward-cache']}). Then serve the pages without 'Cache-Control: no-store'. gate/serve.js sends no-store on every response, and that keeps every page out of the cache. The host sends HTML as 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate', so real Chrome visitors do get the cache. With real restores, C6i-4 works as wanted (see the C6i-4 item). The shared servers cannot show this behavior.
